task_2.title: PremakeDeps honors requirement traits
task_2.description: Conan 2.19.0 updates PremakeDeps so generated Premake dependency metadata respects Conan requirement traits. Headers-related settings, link information, and runtime binary paths are now propagated only when the corresponding dependency traits are enabled, reducing incorrect transitive exposure in consumer builds.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that PremakeDeps only propagates dependency header metadata, library metadata, and runtime binary directories to generated Premake data when the corresponding Conan requirement traits are enabled.

expectation.grounded: For each dependency handled by PremakeDeps, generated Premake variables must expose includedirs, defines, cflags, cxxflags, sharedlinkflags, and exelinkflags only when the requirement has the headers trait enabled; expose libs and libdirs only when the requirement has the libs trait enabled; and expose bindirs only when the requirement has the run trait enabled. Trait-enabled metadata must continue to be emitted for that dependency and configuration.
expectation.conceptual: Premake consumers should only inherit the parts of a dependency that were actually requested. Header-only usage should provide header-related build information, linkable usage should provide library linkage information, and runtime usage should provide executable or shared-library search paths.

constraints.grounded: Do not suppress unrelated dependency metadata that is not gated by these traits, including system libraries, frameworks, or sysroot data. Do not remove metadata for dependencies whose corresponding headers, libs, or run traits remain enabled.
constraints.conceptual: The change should stop over-propagation without causing supported dependency information to disappear for valid consumer scenarios.

behavior: PremakeDeps now evaluates requirement traits per dependency before populating generated Premake dependency variables.
Header-oriented metadata is no longer propagated when a dependency requirement does not expose headers.
Library names and library search directories are no longer propagated when a dependency requirement does not expose libraries.
Binary directories are no longer propagated when a dependency requirement does not expose runtime artifacts.
System libraries, frameworks, and sysroot information remain available independently of the new headers, libs, and run filtering.
acceptance_criteria: When PremakeDeps generates metadata for a dependency whose requirement disables headers, the generated Premake data should omit that dependency's include directories, preprocessor definitions, compile flags, and link flags.
When PremakeDeps generates metadata for a dependency whose requirement disables libs, the generated Premake data should omit that dependency's library names and library search directories.
When PremakeDeps generates metadata for a dependency whose requirement disables run, the generated Premake data should omit that dependency's binary directories.
When a dependency requirement keeps headers, libs, or run enabled, PremakeDeps should continue emitting the corresponding metadata for that dependency.
When trait-based filtering removes one category of metadata, unaffected metadata such as system libraries, frameworks, and sysroot should still be present.

task_1.title: Expose MesonToolchain built-in Meson options as public overrides
task_1.description: The Meson toolchain update makes several built-in Meson option values directly configurable through public MesonToolchain attributes instead of keeping them private. This lets recipes override generated Meson settings such as build type, language standard, runtime library, static PIC, and default library more easily, while preserving existing configuration precedence for the Meson backend.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that MesonToolchain users can override the generated built-in Meson option values through public attributes before generation, including backend, buildtype, b_ndebug, b_staticpic, default_library, cpp_std, c_std, and b_vscrt, while preserving the expected precedence and default derivation rules.

expectation.grounded: MesonToolchain must expose the generated built-in option fields as public attributes named backend, buildtype, b_ndebug, b_staticpic, default_library, cpp_std, c_std, and b_vscrt. During generation, the rendered Meson values must be taken from those public attributes, except that backend must still be resolved with tools.meson.mesontoolchain:backend taking precedence over the MesonToolchain.backend attribute. The default values for these attributes must remain derived from the existing constructor argument, Conan settings, Conan options, and helper conversions already used for backend, build type, fPIC/static library handling, C/C++ standard selection, and MSVC runtime selection.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to customize the main built-in Meson configuration values by setting documented MesonToolchain attributes before generating the toolchain file. Those overrides should appear in the generated Meson configuration, except when an explicit external configuration for the backend is already defined, in which case that external backend choice should still win.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing default derivation rules for buildtype, b_ndebug, b_staticpic, default_library, cpp_std, c_std, or b_vscrt when the user does not override them. Keep backend defaulting to the constructor-supplied backend or ninja, but continue honoring tools.meson.mesontoolchain:backend over any attribute value at render time. Treat b_ndebug as an independently settable output value once the object has been initialized, rather than recomputing it automatically from later buildtype mutations.
constraints.conceptual: Existing MesonToolchain behavior should remain unchanged for callers who do not set the new public attributes. User overrides should be honored predictably, and configuration sources that already had higher priority must keep that priority. Related options should not silently re-derive themselves after a manual override unless the user changes them explicitly.

behavior: MesonToolchain now exposes backend as a public attribute initialized from the constructor argument or the default backend value.
MesonToolchain now exposes buildtype as a public attribute initialized from Conan build_type mapping to Meson build types.
MesonToolchain now exposes b_ndebug as a public attribute initialized from the initial buildtype-derived assert policy and renders the current attribute value directly.
MesonToolchain now exposes b_staticpic as a public attribute initialized from the existing shared and fPIC option logic and renders the current attribute value directly.
MesonToolchain now exposes default_library as a public attribute initialized from the shared option and renders the current attribute value directly.
MesonToolchain now exposes cpp_std and c_std as public attributes initialized from the existing standard-conversion helpers and renders the current attribute values directly.
MesonToolchain now exposes b_vscrt as a public attribute initialized from the existing MSVC runtime helper logic for supported compilers and renders the current attribute value directly.
When generating the toolchain, backend continues to honor the tools.meson.mesontoolchain:backend configuration as higher priority than the MesonToolchain.backend attribute.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe instantiates MesonToolchain and assigns new values to buildtype, default_library, b_ndebug, b_staticpic, cpp_std, c_std, or b_vscrt before generation, the generated Meson toolchain should reflect those assigned values.
When a recipe assigns MesonToolchain.backend and no higher-priority backend configuration is defined, the generated Meson toolchain should use the assigned backend value.
When tools.meson.mesontoolchain:backend is configured, generating the Meson toolchain should use that configured backend even if MesonToolchain.backend was set to a different value.

When a caller does not override the exposed attributes, MesonToolchain should continue generating the same defaults derived from settings, options, constructor input, and existing helper conversions as before this update.
When buildtype is changed after MesonToolchain initialization, b_ndebug should remain whatever explicit or previously derived value is currently stored unless the caller also changes b_ndebug.

task_3.title: Support CMake target aliases in CMakeConfigDeps
task_3.description: Conan 2.19.0 adds support for declaring additional CMake alias target names through `cmake_target_aliases` in CMakeConfigDeps. Generated package and component targets can now expose alternate names, including for renamed root targets, while Conan rejects alias declarations that would conflict with existing generated target names or the resolved root target.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps exposes additional consumer-facing CMake target aliases for packages and components through `cmake_target_aliases`, so projects upgrading to Conan 2.19.0 can preserve or introduce alternate target names without changing the primary target identity. Ensure that invalid alias definitions are rejected before generating ambiguous or conflicting CMake targets.

expectation.grounded: `CMakeConfigDeps` should read the `cmake_target_aliases` property as a list for both package-level and component-level targets and emit corresponding CMake ALIAS targets for the resolved generated target. Package-level aliases must also apply when the root package target is an auto-generated INTERFACE aggregate, and aliases must resolve to a custom `cmake_target_name` when one is configured. Alias definitions that duplicate another alias, match an existing generated target name, or reuse the resolved root target name must raise `ConanException` instead of producing CMake output.
expectation.conceptual: Consumers using `find_package` should be able to reference additional supported target names for a package or one of its components, and those names should behave as aliases to the real Conan-generated target. The feature must preserve the existing primary target naming contract and fail early when alias names would make target resolution ambiguous or invalid.

constraints.grounded: Aliases are additive names only; they must not replace the primary root target, which continues to be controlled by `cmake_target_name`. Validation must prevent duplicate aliases within the same dependency, alias-to-target name collisions, and alias names that equal the resolved root target name. Generated CMake should only declare an alias target when that alias target does not already exist.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change the canonical target name or link behavior just because alternate names are added. Reject conflicting alias configurations and avoid generating duplicate CMake target declarations.

behavior: `cmake_target_aliases` on a package creates extra CMake target names that alias the package's root Conan target.
`cmake_target_aliases` on a component creates extra CMake target names that alias that specific component target.
When `cmake_target_name` changes the root target name, any declared aliases point to the renamed root target rather than redefining the primary target.
Package-level aliases remain available even when the package root target is synthesized as an INTERFACE target that aggregates component targets.
If two aliases repeat the same name, if an alias matches an existing generated target name, or if an alias equals the resolved root target name, Conan stops generation with `ConanException`.
Generated CMake alias targets are conditionally declared only when the alias target is not already present in the consumer's CMake target graph.
acceptance_criteria: When a package declares one or more package-level `cmake_target_aliases` and a consumer runs `find_package`, the consumer should be able to reference each alias as a valid CMake target for the package.
When a component declares one or more `cmake_target_aliases`, each alias should resolve to that component target and not to an unrelated package target.
When a package defines both `cmake_target_name` and `cmake_target_aliases`, the configured `cmake_target_name` should remain the primary generated target and the aliases should resolve to it.
When a package exposes components and its root package target is auto-generated as an aggregate interface target, package-level aliases should still resolve to that root target.

When alias names are duplicated, collide with an existing generated target name, or reuse the resolved root target name, dependency generation should fail with `ConanException` instead of producing conflicting CMake targets.
When an alias target name already exists in CMake, the generated package configuration should not attempt to redeclare that alias target.

task_4.title: Expose conan_data in serialized ConanFile output
task_4.description: Conan 2.19.0 adds recipe conan data to serialized ConanFile metadata so commands that expose serialized recipe information can show the structured data defined by the recipe. This is an additive visibility change intended to make conan_data inspectable without changing output for recipes that do not provide it.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that recipe conan data becomes visible in user-facing serialized Conan metadata so users can inspect the data attached to a recipe through commands such as `conan graph info` and other outputs built from serialized `ConanFile` information.

expectation.grounded: When a `ConanFile` has non-empty `self.conan_data`, its serialized representation should include a `conandata` field containing that structured data. Commands that render serialized `ConanFile` information, including `conan graph info`, should surface the same `conandata` content in their output.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to see a recipe's conan data anywhere Conan already exposes serialized recipe metadata. If a recipe has no meaningful conan data, command output should remain unchanged.

constraints.grounded: The change should be additive: existing serialized fields and their meaning must remain intact, and `conandata` should appear only when `self.conan_data` is present with content. The serialized `conandata` value should preserve the recipe data structure rather than transforming it into a different shape.
constraints.conceptual: Do not regress existing metadata output. Only expose recipe conan data when it actually exists, and present it in the same structure users defined.

behavior: Serialized `ConanFile` metadata now includes a top-level `conandata` entry when the recipe provides non-empty `self.conan_data`.
`conan graph info` now exposes recipe conan data as part of the serialized recipe or node information it returns.
Any other command output that is built from serialized `ConanFile` data will also include `conandata` for recipes that define it.
Recipes with missing, empty, or falsey conan data continue to serialize without a `conandata` field.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe defines non-empty `self.conan_data`, running `conan graph info` in a serialized or machine-readable form should include a `conandata` section containing the same nested data.
When Conan produces serialized `ConanFile` metadata for a recipe that has non-empty `self.conan_data`, the serialized result should contain a `conandata` field instead of omitting that recipe data.
When a recipe does not provide conan data, or the conan data is empty, serialized outputs should not introduce a `conandata` field and existing metadata should remain otherwise unchanged.

task_5.title: Associate `conan source` backup sources with recipe references
task_5.description: Conan 2.19.0 improves backup source tracking by recording backup sources generated by `conan source` under a derived recipe reference when the recipe declares enough identifying information. This makes those backup sources attributable to the recipe reference more often, while preserving the existing fallback for recipes that still cannot be identified.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that backup sources generated by `conan source` are associated with a meaningful recipe reference whenever the recipe defines enough identity information, so users can manage those backup sources through normal reference-based Conan workflows instead of relying only on a generic fallback bucket.

expectation.grounded: When backup source metadata is generated and `conanfile.ref` is not available, Conan should derive the reference key from `ConanFile.name` and `ConanFile.version`, and include `@user` and `/channel` when those public recipe attributes are defined. If the recipe does not provide both `name` and `version`, Conan should continue to register the backup source under the existing `unknown` reference bucket. Backup sources created under one derived reference should not be automatically reassigned to a later different reference, and `conan cache backup-upload` must remain a valid way to upload backup sources that are not linked to the desired reference.
expectation.conceptual: When users run `conan source` on a recipe that identifies itself, Conan should remember downloaded backup sources under that recipe reference so later Conan operations can recognize them more naturally. Recipes that still do not provide enough identity should keep the previous fallback behavior, and explicitly uploading backup sources should remain possible when the stored reference does not match the later recipe reference.

constraints.grounded: Do not require an already bound `conanfile.ref` to create a reference-aware backup source entry when `name` and `version` are available. Do not synthesize a partial or ambiguous reference when either `name` or `version` is missing. Preserve optional `user` and `channel` components only when present, preserve the `unknown` fallback for insufficiently identified recipes, and keep distinct references isolated rather than merging old backup sources into a new reference automatically.
constraints.conceptual: Only complete recipe identities should produce reference-based backup source associations. Incomplete identities should still use the generic fallback, and backup sources tied to one recipe reference should not be silently treated as belonging to a different reference later.

behavior: If `conan source` generates backup source metadata for a recipe without an available bound recipe reference, Conan now derives the backup source reference from the recipe's declared `name/version` identity.
If the recipe also declares `user` and/or `channel`, Conan includes those components in the derived backup source reference.
If the recipe does not declare both `name` and `version`, Conan continues to store the backup source under the generic `unknown` reference bucket.
Backup sources recorded under one derived reference are not automatically linked to a later different recipe reference.
Backup sources that remain under `unknown` or under an older different reference can still be uploaded through `conan cache backup-upload`.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe defines `name` and `version` and `conan source` generates backup sources without an existing bound recipe reference, the stored backup-source association should use that `name/version` reference instead of `unknown`.
When the same recipe also defines `user` and/or `channel`, the stored backup-source association should reflect the full reference including those optional components.
When a recipe executed with `conan source` does not define both `name` and `version`, backup-source association should continue to fall back to `unknown`.
When backup sources were generated under one reference and the recipe is later used with a different reference, Conan should not implicitly reassign the original backup sources to the new reference.
When backup sources are not associated with the desired reference, users should still be able to upload them with `conan cache backup-upload`.

task_6.title: Include Conan user and channel in CycloneDX SBOM references
task_6.description: CycloneDX SBOM generation now includes Conan package namespace information in generated package references. This makes component and dependency identifiers reflect user and channel when those values exist, improving uniqueness and traceability without changing references for packages that do not use them.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CycloneDX SBOM references include Conan package user and channel information when available so packages published under different namespaces are uniquely identified in component and dependency references.

expectation.grounded: For CycloneDX 1.4 and 1.6 SBOM generation, compute package references consistently across `components[].bom-ref`, `metadata.component.bom-ref`, `dependencies[].ref`, and `dependencies[].dependsOn` using the Conan package name, version, and recipe revision, and append the package `user` and `channel` when they are present. If the SBOM uses an existing synthetic root reference instead of a package-derived root reference, keep using that synthetic root reference.
expectation.conceptual: Generated CycloneDX documents should expose the full Conan package identity in their reference fields, including namespace information when it exists, so downstream SBOM consumers can distinguish otherwise similar packages and follow dependency links correctly.

constraints.grounded: Do not change which components or dependency edges are emitted by CycloneDX SBOM generation. Do not emit empty namespace placeholders when `user` or `channel` is absent. Preserve the prior reference format for packages that have no `user` and no `channel`, and preserve the existing synthetic top-level root identifier behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be additive and backward-compatible for packages without namespace information, and it should only refine identifier content rather than alter the SBOM structure or dependency graph.

behavior: CycloneDX 1.4 component `bom-ref` values include Conan `user` when present and Conan `channel` when present, in addition to the existing package name, version, and recipe revision information.
CycloneDX 1.6 component `bom-ref` values follow the same namespace-aware reference format as CycloneDX 1.4.
Dependency references use the same namespace-aware identifier format for each `dependencies[].ref` entry and each `dependsOn` target, keeping dependency links aligned with component identifiers.
The metadata component reference for a normal root package uses the same namespace-aware identifier format, while synthetic root references remain unchanged.
Packages that do not define a Conan `user` or `channel` continue to produce references without those fields.
acceptance_criteria: When generating a CycloneDX 1.4 SBOM for a package with a Conan `user` but no `channel`, the package reference fields should include the `user` and should not include an empty `channel` value.
When generating a CycloneDX 1.4 or 1.6 SBOM for a package with both Conan `user` and `channel`, the same namespace-aware reference should appear consistently in component and dependency sections.
When generating a CycloneDX 1.4 or 1.6 SBOM for packages without Conan namespace information, the reference fields should remain in the pre-existing name/version/revision form.
When a generated SBOM uses a synthetic top-level root reference, that root reference should remain synthetic rather than being replaced by a package-derived namespace-aware reference.

task_8.title: Add GCC 12.5 settings support
task_8.description: The library now recognizes GCC 12.5 as a supported compiler version in its built-in settings model, allowing users to configure and use that compiler release without version-validation failures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that GCC 12.5 is recognized as a supported compiler setting so users can declare and use that toolchain version without configuration rejection.

expectation.grounded: The default settings model must accept `compiler=gcc` with `compiler.version=12.5` as a valid setting value. This support should be available anywhere the public compiler settings are parsed or validated through the standard Conan settings definition.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading to this version should be able to specify GCC 12.5 in normal compiler configuration and have the library treat it as a supported GCC release.

constraints.grounded: The change is additive to the allowed GCC version values only. Existing supported GCC versions must remain valid, and validation behavior for other compilers or unrelated settings must not change.
constraints.conceptual: Support for GCC 12.5 should extend current behavior without altering how previously supported compiler versions or other settings work.

behavior: `compiler.version=12.5` is a valid setting when `compiler=gcc` is selected.
Commands and workflows that rely on the built-in settings definition accept GCC 12.5 instead of rejecting it as an unsupported GCC version.
Previously supported GCC version values continue to be accepted unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given the standard settings model, when a user configures `compiler=gcc` and `compiler.version=12.5`, the configuration should be accepted as valid.
When a profile or command uses GCC 12.5 through standard compiler settings, it should proceed past settings validation without an unsupported-version failure.
When users configure any GCC version that was already supported before this update, it should continue to behave the same as before.

task_7.title: Honor test_package_folder in conan export-pkg
task_7.description: The upgrade enables `conan export-pkg` to honor a recipe's custom `test_package_folder` setting so package export flows can automatically find and use non-default test package locations without requiring a separate command-line override.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan export-pkg` recognizes a recipe-defined custom test package folder so packages using `test_package_folder` behave consistently during export packaging, while still allowing an explicit command-line test folder override.

expectation.grounded: When `conan export-pkg` processes a recipe, it should resolve the test package location from the recipe's `test_package_folder` attribute if `--test-folder` is not provided. If `--test-folder` is provided, that explicit command-line value should take precedence over the recipe attribute. When a test package is resolved through either mechanism, `conan export-pkg` should use it in the command's existing test-package execution flow.
expectation.conceptual: Users who place their test package in a custom folder declared by the recipe should be able to run `conan export-pkg` without extra configuration and have the command pick up that test package automatically. If a user explicitly names a test folder on the command line, that choice should override the recipe's default.

constraints.grounded: Do not require `--test-folder` for recipes that already declare `test_package_folder`. Preserve the precedence of an explicit `--test-folder` value over recipe metadata. Preserve existing behavior for recipes that do not declare `test_package_folder`, including normal default test package discovery and cases where no test package is used.
constraints.conceptual: The new support should extend custom-folder discovery without breaking current export flows. Explicit user input should still win, and projects that rely on the default test package layout should continue to behave the same way as before.

behavior: `conan export-pkg` now consults the recipe's `test_package_folder` attribute when no `--test-folder` override is supplied.
A recipe that declares a non-default test package folder can have that location automatically discovered and used by `conan export-pkg`.
If `--test-folder` is passed to `conan export-pkg`, the command uses that value instead of the recipe's `test_package_folder` attribute.
Recipes without a `test_package_folder` declaration retain the prior default behavior for test package lookup during `conan export-pkg`.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recipe that defines `test_package_folder` with a custom location, when `conan export-pkg` runs without `--test-folder`, then it should resolve and use that custom test package location.
Given a recipe with a custom `test_package_folder`, when `conan export-pkg` finds that test package, then the command should include it in its normal post-export test-package flow.
Given a recipe that defines `test_package_folder`, when `conan export-pkg` is invoked with `--test-folder`, then the command-line location should be used instead of the recipe attribute.
Given a recipe that does not define `test_package_folder`, when `conan export-pkg` runs, then default test package discovery behavior should remain unchanged.

task_9.title: Support custom makefile names in Autotools build and install flows
task_9.description: Conan 2.19.0 adds an opt-in way to tell the Autotools helper which makefile to use during build and install operations. This lets consumers work with projects that do not use the default Makefile name while preserving existing behavior for standard Autotools workflows.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Autotools-based package builds and installs can target a custom makefile name instead of requiring the default Makefile, while preserving existing behavior when no custom makefile is specified.

expectation.grounded: The public `conan.tools.gnu.Autotools` helper should accept an optional `makefile` argument on both `Autotools.make()` and `Autotools.install()`. When that argument is provided, the helper should run the underlying `make` command against the specified makefile rather than relying on the default file name. `Autotools.install()` should pass the same makefile selection through to `make`, keep its install-target behavior, and continue to add `DESTDIR` automatically when the caller has not already supplied it.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to build and install Autotools projects through the public helper API even when the project uses a non-default makefile name. The new option should work consistently for both build and install operations, and existing calls that do not use it should behave exactly as before.

constraints.grounded: This capability must remain additive and backward compatible. Calls that omit `makefile` must keep the existing make invocation behavior. Existing `target`, `args`, parallel job handling, and automatic `DESTDIR` insertion in `Autotools.install()` must continue to behave the same way aside from optionally selecting a different makefile.
constraints.conceptual: The feature must be opt-in, must not disrupt standard Autotools packaging flows, and must not alter normal build or install semantics except for choosing a different makefile when explicitly requested.

behavior: `Autotools.make()` accepts a new optional `makefile` parameter.
When `makefile` is provided to `Autotools.make()`, the generated `make` invocation explicitly uses that file.
`Autotools.install()` accepts the same optional `makefile` parameter and forwards it to the underlying `make` invocation.
`Autotools.install()` continues to default to the install target and still injects `DESTDIR` when the caller has not supplied one.
If no custom makefile is provided, both build and install flows continue using the default makefile resolution behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer calls `Autotools.make()` with a custom `makefile`, the build should run against that makefile instead of requiring the default `Makefile` name.
When a consumer calls `Autotools.install()` with a custom `makefile`, the install flow should use that makefile and still execute the install target.
When a consumer calls `Autotools.install()` without supplying `DESTDIR`, installation should continue to stage into the package folder even when a custom makefile is selected.
When no custom `makefile` is passed, existing Autotools build and install behavior should remain unchanged.

task_10.title: Improve HTML graph and diff search usability
task_10.description: The update improves the usability of generated HTML graph and diff views by reducing repeated redraw or filter work while users type, surfacing empty-search feedback in diff reports, and allowing graph search to move focus to a matched package when Enter is pressed.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that generated HTML graph and diff reports provide more usable search interactions by delaying repeated updates while users type, keeping visible navigation and content synchronized, showing when a diff search returns no matches, and letting users focus a searched package from the graph search box by pressing Enter.

expectation.grounded: Generated HTML from the graph formatter should debounce redraws triggered by the package search and exclude-package inputs, and when the package search field receives the Enter key it should focus a package node that matches the current search. Generated HTML from the diff report formatter should debounce include and exclude search filtering, apply visibility changes consistently to both sidebar entries and their associated diff-content sections, expose a visible searching state while filtering is in progress, and show a visible no-results indicator when the current queries leave no matching files.
expectation.conceptual: HTML report search should stay responsive on large outputs without reprocessing on every keystroke. Diff pages should clearly reflect whether anything matches the current filters, and graph search should let users jump directly to a matching package from the keyboard.

constraints.grounded: Debouncing must only change when filtering or redraw happens, not the meaning of the existing search or exclude inputs. In the diff HTML view, sidebar visibility and content-panel visibility must remain synchronized for every file under the current queries. In the graph HTML view, automatic focus should occur only when Enter is pressed in the package search field and only if the current search matches at least one package node.
constraints.conceptual: These UX changes must preserve existing search semantics, avoid surprising navigation during normal typing, and never leave the report navigation out of sync with the content being shown.

behavior: HTML diff report include and exclude searches are applied after a short debounce instead of on every input event.
Diff filtering now hides or shows each sidebar file entry together with its corresponding diff section.
The diff HTML view shows a visible searching indicator while a filter pass is running.
The diff HTML view shows a visible empty-result indicator when the current include and exclude queries leave no visible files.
HTML graph package search and exclude-package updates are applied after a short debounce before the graph redraw runs.
Pressing Enter in the HTML graph package search triggers an immediate redraw that focuses a package node matching the current search, when such a node exists.
acceptance_criteria: When a user types into the HTML diff include or exclude search boxes, the visible results should update only after a brief pause rather than on every keystroke.
When a diff file does not match the current include or exclude criteria, its sidebar link and its diff section should both be hidden; when it matches, both should be shown.
When the current diff search criteria match no files, the page should display a visible no-results indication.
When a user types into the HTML graph search or exclude inputs, the graph should redraw only after a brief pause rather than on every keystroke.
When a user presses Enter in the HTML graph search input and the current query matches a package, the graph view should move focus to a matching package node.

task_11.title: Premake Windows platform override support
task_11.description: Conan 2.19.0 updates the Premake integration for Windows so Visual Studio-based builds can request a custom MSBuild platform, while generated Premake toolchain references use a path format that Premake can resolve correctly on Windows. This improves Windows compatibility without changing the existing non-MSBuild build flow.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's Premake integration on Windows allows consumers to choose a custom MSBuild platform for Visual Studio-based Premake builds and that generated Premake toolchain references remain consumable with Windows paths, without regressing existing Premake behavior on other actions.

expectation.grounded: The `Premake.build()` API should support an optional `msbuild_platform` argument. When the selected Premake action targets Visual Studio (`vs...`), providing `msbuild_platform` should cause the underlying `MSBuild` invocation for `<workspace>.sln` to use that platform value while preserving existing `targets` handling. `Premake.configure()` should render the `PremakeToolchain` Lua reference with a normalized path format that Premake can resolve on Windows. If the `PremakeToolchain` output is missing, `Premake.build()` should continue to raise `ConanException` instead of building.
expectation.conceptual: When using Conan's Premake support on Windows, developers should be able to explicitly select the platform label that Visual Studio or MSBuild uses for the generated solution, and the generated Premake files should work with Windows path syntax without manual fixes. Existing usage that does not request a custom platform should keep working as before.

constraints.grounded: The new platform override must be optional and only affect Visual Studio-backed Premake actions. Non-Visual-Studio actions must continue using the existing make-based flow, including current build-type, job, and verbosity behavior. The build must still depend on a generated `PremakeToolchain` file and must not silently proceed when that prerequisite is absent.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be backward compatible for current Premake consumers. It should add Windows-specific configurability and path compatibility without altering how other Premake actions build or weakening existing failure behavior when required generated files are missing.

behavior: Adds an optional `msbuild_platform` parameter to `Premake.build()`.
For Visual Studio Premake actions, `msbuild_platform` overrides the platform passed to the underlying MSBuild solution build.
For non-Visual-Studio Premake actions, the existing make-based build path remains in effect and the platform override does not change execution.
The generated Premake Lua file now references the Conan Premake toolchain using a normalized path representation that avoids Windows separator issues.
Calling `Premake.build()` without an available `PremakeToolchain` file still fails with `ConanException`.
acceptance_criteria: When a Windows consumer runs a Visual Studio-based Premake build and passes `msbuild_platform` to `Premake.build()`, the resulting solution build should target that platform value.
When `msbuild_platform` is not provided, Visual Studio-based Premake builds should retain the prior default platform selection behavior.
When Conan generates the Premake Lua entry that loads the Premake toolchain on Windows, the referenced path should be accepted by Premake without manual path rewriting.
When `Premake.build()` is used with a non-Visual-Studio Premake action, build execution should remain on the existing make-based path.
When the required `PremakeToolchain` output has not been generated, `Premake.build()` should raise `ConanException` instead of running a build.

task_12.title: Support composing compatible Conan runner profiles
task_12.description: Conan 2.19.0 lets runner configuration participate in profile composition so users can split compatible runner settings across multiple profiles. Composed profiles now merge runner data when the runner type is consistent and fail fast when different runner types are combined.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan profile composition supports runner-enabled profiles by combining compatible runner configuration across profiles and rejecting incompatible runner type combinations.

expectation.grounded: When Conan composes profiles, the `runner` section must be included in the composed profile. If multiple profiles define `runner.type` with the same value, the resulting profile should keep that runner type and merge the remaining runner keys across the composed profiles. If multiple profiles define different `runner.type` values, composition must fail with a `ConanException` instead of silently overriding one runner with another.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to split runner settings across multiple composed profiles as long as those profiles refer to the same kind of runner. If composed profiles request different runner kinds, Conan should stop and report the configuration conflict.

constraints.grounded: Profile composition must continue to work when only one profile provides a runner type or when additional runner fields are added by another profile without changing the explicit `runner.type`. Conan must not silently replace one explicit runner type with a different explicit runner type during composition.
constraints.conceptual: Composing profiles should remain predictable: compatible runner settings can be combined, but incompatible runner declarations must never be auto-resolved by implicitly picking one.

behavior: Runner-enabled profiles are supported in profile composition scenarios.
If composed profiles declare the same `runner.type`, Conan merges their runner configuration into one effective runner definition.
If only one side of the composition defines the runner type, the resulting profile keeps that runner and incorporates other non-conflicting runner settings.
If composed profiles declare different `runner.type` values, Conan raises a `ConanException` during profile composition.
acceptance_criteria: When a user composes profiles that define runner settings for the same `runner.type`, Conan should accept the composition and expose a single combined runner configuration.
When a user composes a runner profile with another profile that adds more runner options without changing the runner type, Conan should preserve the selected runner and apply the added options.
When a user composes profiles that specify different `runner.type` values, Conan should fail profile composition with a configuration error instead of selecting one runner implicitly.
When no conflicting runner types are introduced, runner-aware profile composition should not change the expected behavior of composing other profile data.

task_13.title: Explicitly reject Conan channel values without a user
task_13.description: Conan 2.19.0 turns an invalid recipe reference state into an explicit user-facing validation error: if a channel is provided without a user, the command now fails early with a clear ConanException instead of falling through to a lower-level failure path.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan rejects any recipe reference that specifies a `channel` without a corresponding `user`, and reports a clear user-facing error instead of allowing the operation to continue into a lower-level failure.

expectation.grounded: After applying recipe-defined values and any CLI overrides such as `--user` and `--channel`, Conan must validate that `channel` is not set unless `user` is also set. If `conanfile.channel` is present while `conanfile.user` is absent, the operation must raise `ConanException` immediately, before further recipe processing or `RecipeReference` creation, and the error should identify the invalid channel value.
expectation.conceptual: Any Conan operation that resolves a recipe reference must treat `channel` as dependent on `user`: a standalone channel is invalid, and the command should stop immediately with a clear configuration error rather than an assertion or ambiguous failure.

constraints.grounded: Do not change valid reference combinations: recipes with neither `user` nor `channel`, with `user` only, or with both `user` and `channel` must continue to work. The validation must apply consistently whether the values come from recipe attributes or CLI-provided overrides, and providing a valid `user` must make a `channel` acceptable.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve normal recipe reference behavior and only reject the invalid case where a channel exists without a user, regardless of how those values were supplied.

behavior: Conan now performs an explicit validation after user and channel values have been resolved onto the recipe.
If a recipe has a `channel` but no `user`, Conan raises `ConanException` immediately during recipe loading.
The reported validation error includes the offending channel value so the invalid reference is easier to identify.
The invalid channel-without-user condition is rejected before Conan proceeds with later recipe processing, avoiding lower-level failure behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs a Conan command with `--channel` set and no `--user`, it should fail with `ConanException` explaining that the specified channel cannot be used without a user.
When a recipe declares a `channel` but no `user`, Conan should stop immediately with the same validation error when the recipe is loaded for reference-based operations.
When a recipe provides a `user` and no `channel`, Conan should continue to process the recipe normally.
When a valid `user` is present and a `channel` is supplied, Conan should accept the reference and continue the operation normally.
When the invalid channel-without-user condition is detected, Conan should fail before continuing into later recipe processing stages.

task_15.title: Always show remote login credential prompts
task_15.description: Version 2.19.0 fixes interactive remote authentication so username and password prompts are not hidden by log verbosity settings. It also preserves readable prompt rendering when output carries a scope or prefix, preventing login flows from appearing to stall without visible credential requests.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that interactive remote authentication always shows the username and password request prompts even when normal output is filtered by the selected verbosity level, so users can complete login without hidden credential requests.

expectation.grounded: During the remote login credential request flow, the prompt that asks for the remote username and the prompt that asks for the password must be emitted through output that is not suppressed by verbosity filtering. If a username is already provided, the flow should skip the username question and still show the password prompt. Prompt rendering should remain complete and readable when output scope or prefix formatting is active.
expectation.conceptual: Whenever the CLI needs credentials for a remote, the user must always see the prompt telling them what value to enter. Lower verbosity settings must not hide these interactive prompts, and providing a username up front should only leave the password prompt visible.

constraints.grounded: This change should affect only the visibility and formatting of interactive credential prompts. It must not alter when interactivity is required, how usernames and passwords are collected, or the authentication result. Username prompting should remain conditional on the username being absent, and the prompts should continue to behave like inline terminal prompts rather than unrelated log lines.
constraints.conceptual: Only the prompt visibility issue should change. The login flow, credential handling, and overall authentication behavior should stay the same apart from making the prompts reliably visible and readable.

behavior: Interactive credential prompts for remote login are displayed even when the configured verbosity would normally hide standard output messages.
The remote username prompt is shown only when no username was supplied to the login flow.
The password prompt remains visible for the targeted remote and user regardless of verbosity filtering.
When message scope or prefix formatting is active, the credential prompt is rendered as a complete readable prompt instead of being partially hidden or malformed.
acceptance_criteria: When a user starts an interactive remote login under a reduced verbosity level, the CLI should still display the prompt requesting the remote username if no username was provided.
When the login flow proceeds to password entry, the CLI should still display the password prompt under the same reduced verbosity settings.
When a username is supplied before password entry, the CLI should not ask for the username again and should still display the password prompt.
When scoped output formatting is enabled for the command, the credential prompt should remain fully readable on the terminal and usable for inline input.

task_14.title: Validate required Conan version before loading hooks
task_14.description: Conan 2.19.0 now checks the configured required Conan version during startup before loading hooks, so unsupported clients fail fast with the version requirement instead of surfacing hook-loading failures first. Hook-backed operations continue to share consistent hook state across install, export, graph, local, and report flows, and that state is refreshed when the API is reinitialized.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan validates `core:required_conan_version` before loading hooks so users with an unsupported Conan version receive the version compatibility failure immediately and hook-loading problems cannot mask it.

expectation.grounded: During `ConanAPI` initialization, evaluate `core:required_conan_version` from configuration before hook discovery/loading. If the running Conan version does not satisfy the configured range, API and CLI initialization should stop with the required-version failure before any hook-loading failure is raised. When initialization succeeds, hook-aware flows including install, export, graph binary evaluation, local source/build execution, generator writing, and report source configuration should continue to use a shared hook manager, and `ConanAPI.reinit()` should reload that hook state for subsequent operations.
expectation.conceptual: Conan should fail fast on version incompatibility before hooks influence startup, while normal hook-enabled commands should keep working consistently and pick up refreshed hook configuration after reinitialization.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress successful startup when `core:required_conan_version` is satisfied. Existing hook-driven behavior in install, system requirements, source installation, export, graph resolution, local source/build, generator generation, and report diff source setup should remain available after initialization, and reinitialization should refresh hooks instead of keeping stale registrations.
constraints.conceptual: Supported environments should see the same hook-based behavior as before, and refreshing configuration should consistently apply updated hooks without requiring a new process.

behavior: `core:required_conan_version` is checked during Conan startup before hooks are loaded.
If the configured required version is not satisfied, Conan aborts before hook-loading errors can override or hide the version incompatibility.
Hook-aware operations share a consistent initialized hook state across install, export, graph, local, and report-related flows.
After API reinitialization, later hook-aware operations use reloaded hooks instead of stale hook registrations.
acceptance_criteria: When `core:required_conan_version` excludes the running Conan version, a command that initializes Conan should fail immediately because of the version mismatch.
When hooks are invalid or fail to load but `core:required_conan_version` is already incompatible, the user should still see the version incompatibility outcome rather than a hook-loading failure.
When the running Conan version satisfies `core:required_conan_version`, commands that rely on hooks should continue to initialize and run with hook support.
When hook configuration changes and the API is reinitialized, subsequent hook-aware operations should observe the refreshed hook state.

task_16.title: Support spaced compiler paths in auto-detection
task_16.description: Conan 2.19.0 fixes compiler and profile auto-detection so configured compiler executables with spaces in their path can still be invoked correctly, and it improves `cc` version parsing for version strings that include extra build metadata or more version segments.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that compiler/profile auto-detection works when the configured compiler executable path contains spaces, and that compiler version detection remains accurate for `cc` outputs that include extra build metadata or extended numeric version formats.

expectation.grounded: During compiler and profile auto-detection, Conan should successfully invoke compiler executables supplied to `detect_libcxx()`, `_cc_compiler()`, `detect_gcc_compiler()`, `detect_clang_compiler()`, `detect_intel_compiler()`, and `detect_suncc_compiler()` even when the executable path or configured command contains spaces. `_cc_compiler()` should continue identifying `gcc` versus `clang`, and it should extract the version from `cc --version` output when the first version line contains leading parenthesized build information or any number of dot-separated numeric components.
expectation.conceptual: Compiler auto-detection should behave the same for compiler binaries located in paths with spaces as it does for ordinary paths. Users should still get correct compiler-family detection, standard library inference where applicable, and version detection from common `cc --version` formats that include extra metadata.

constraints.grounded: The change should preserve existing detection outcomes for supported compiler families, including `gcc`, `clang`, Apple clang frontends, `intel-cc`, and `sun-cc`. Detection helpers should continue returning an undetected result when the underlying compiler command fails, and `detect_libcxx()` should keep using the compiler probe outcome to distinguish standard library variants without regressing existing successful flows.
constraints.conceptual: This update should make auto-detection more robust without changing normal detection results for already supported compilers. Failed compiler invocations should still fail cleanly rather than being misclassified, and existing successful detections should remain stable.

behavior: Compiler detection commands now execute the configured compiler executable as a single command value, so paths containing spaces no longer break version or probe invocation.

The standard library probe used during compiler detection applies the same executable handling, allowing libc++ versus libstdc++ inference to proceed for compilers whose executable path contains spaces.
`_cc_compiler()` can parse `cc --version` output when build metadata in parentheses appears before the numeric version.
`_cc_compiler()` can capture versions with multiple dot-separated components instead of assuming only one or two numeric segments.
If a compiler version or probe command returns a non-zero exit code, the detection helpers still report the compiler as undetected rather than forcing a detection result.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan auto-detects a profile with a configured `cc` compiler path that contains spaces, it should complete compiler detection without failing because the executable path was split incorrectly.

When a compiler executable path containing spaces is used for version checks or compiler probing, Conan should still identify the correct compiler family and continue any applicable standard library inference.
When `cc --version` output begins with parenthesized build metadata before the version number, Conan should still extract the compiler version correctly.
When `cc --version` reports a version with more than two dot-separated numeric components, Conan should preserve the full detected numeric version.
When the compiler cannot be executed successfully, Conan should continue to report the compiler as undetected instead of misclassifying it.

task_17.title: Fix untargz for Windows long-path destinations
task_17.description: Conan 2.19.0 fixes tar extraction to Windows destinations that use the `\\?\` long-path prefix. `untargz()` should correctly extract archives with nested paths into those destinations, including with and without root stripping, instead of failing because Windows long-path handling does not normalize forward slashes in archive member names.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `untargz()` can extract tar archives into Windows destination paths that use the `\\?\` long-path prefix without failing, while preserving the expected extracted directory structure when root stripping is enabled or disabled.

expectation.grounded: When `untargz(filename, destination=...)` receives a destination beginning with the Windows long-path prefix `\\?\`, tar extraction must succeed even though archive entries use `/`-separated member names. The function should no longer surface the Windows path-syntax `OSError` caused by mixed separators, and it should preserve normal `untargz()` behavior for both `strip_root=true` and `strip_root=false`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to unpack tar archives into Windows long-path locations with `untargz()` the same way they can into normal paths. The extraction should complete successfully and create the expected files and folders instead of failing on path-format issues.

constraints.grounded: Do not change observable extraction behavior for destinations that do not use the `\\?\` prefix. Existing `untargz()` semantics for archive layout, optional root stripping, and member selection should remain consistent; the fix should only address long-path handling and separator normalization needed for those destinations.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to the Windows long-path edge case and must not alter how tar extraction behaves for standard paths or change the resulting archive layout beyond making long-path extraction work correctly.

behavior: `untargz()` must treat Windows destinations beginning with `\\?\` as a supported extraction target instead of failing during tar extraction.
For `\\?\` destinations, tar members with nested `/`-separated paths must be extracted into the correct Windows directory hierarchy without triggering a path-syntax failure.
The corrected behavior must apply whether `strip_root` is enabled or disabled, so the extracted tree matches the requested root-handling mode.
acceptance_criteria: When `untargz()` extracts a tar archive to a Windows destination prefixed with `\\?\`, it should complete without raising the path-format `OSError` caused by mixed path separators.
When `strip_root=true` and the archive contains a single top-level root folder, extraction to a `\\?\` destination should place the root's contents directly under the destination.
When `strip_root=false`, extraction to a `\\?\` destination should preserve the archive's top-level root folder under the destination.
When the destination does not use the Windows long-path prefix, `untargz()` should continue to behave as before.

task_19.title: Fix concurrent startup in self-contained Conan binaries
task_19.description: Conan 2.19.0 fixes a runtime compatibility issue in self-contained standalone binaries so concurrent operations start correctly when Conan is packaged as a frozen executable such as a PyInstaller build.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan distributed as a self-contained executable can start and run concurrent operations correctly, instead of failing because frozen-binary process startup is not initialized properly.

expectation.grounded: When the Conan CLI entry point runs from a frozen or self-contained executable, it should initialize Python multiprocessing in a frozen-application-compatible way before continuing into the normal `run()` startup flow, so commands that depend on Conan's concurrent execution model behave correctly.
expectation.conceptual: Users running Conan as a packaged standalone binary should see the same successful startup and concurrent command behavior they would expect from a normal Conan installation, without special failures caused by the packaging format.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to startup compatibility for frozen/self-contained Conan executables. Standard CLI invocation must continue through the existing entry point and preserve normal command behavior outside this compatibility fix.
constraints.conceptual: The update should remove standalone-binary startup incompatibilities without changing ordinary Conan command semantics or introducing unrelated behavior changes.

behavior: Self-contained or frozen Conan executables now perform multiprocessing-compatible startup before executing the main CLI flow.
Concurrent Conan operations in PyInstaller-style standalone binaries no longer fail solely because the executable was packaged as a frozen application.
After the compatibility startup step, Conan continues into the same command execution path as before.
acceptance_criteria: Given Conan is packaged as a self-contained executable, when a user runs a command that relies on Conan's concurrent execution behavior, it should start and run without frozen-binary multiprocessing bootstrap failures.
Given Conan is invoked through its normal CLI entry point, when startup completes, it should continue into the standard command dispatch flow.
When the standalone Conan binary is executed in the release-note reproduction scenario, it should behave normally instead of failing because of frozen executable startup incompatibility.

task_18.title: Filter application package requirements from generated CMake base targets
task_18.description: Conan 2.19.0 fixes CMakeConfigDeps so application packages are no longer treated as automatically linkable base dependencies in generated CMake targets. This prevents consumer packages from inheriting invalid application target links while preserving explicit component-level dependencies that are intentionally exposed.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps does not automatically propagate package requirements whose dependency has package_type=application as base link dependencies in generated CMake targets, while still honoring explicitly declared component dependencies from those packages.

expectation.grounded: When `CMakeConfigDeps` generates targets for a package that reaches another package through `requires()`, dependencies with `package_type=application` must be filtered out from the auto-derived root target dependency list. The generated root target for the consumer package must therefore stop referencing the application package's default CMake target solely because it appeared in `requires()`. Explicit `cpp_info.requires` references to specific components from that application package must remain represented when those component targets are valid linkable dependencies.
expectation.conceptual: Generated CMake dependency files should not make a library or package link against an executable-style dependency just because it is listed as a normal requirement. If the package explicitly depends on a specific usable component from that dependency, that explicit component relationship should still be preserved.

constraints.grounded: Do not change dependency propagation for non-application packages in `CMakeConfigDeps`. Do not suppress explicitly declared component requirements that point into a package marked as `application`. Preserve existing target naming and normal dependency emission for supported non-application and explicitly requested component targets.
constraints.conceptual: Only the unintended automatic linkage to application packages should be removed. Existing behavior for ordinary package dependencies and intentionally declared component dependencies should continue to work.

behavior: Auto-derived root target dependencies emitted by `CMakeConfigDeps` no longer include the default CMake target of a required package whose `package_type` is `application`.
A package that depends on an application package through `requires()` will stop exposing that application's root target as an inherited link dependency in generated CMake config files.
Explicit component-level dependencies declared by the consuming package remain in generated output even when the referenced package is marked as `application`.
Dependency emission for non-application packages remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given a package generated with `CMakeConfigDeps` that has a `requires()` dependency on a package marked as `application`, when its CMake targets are generated, the package's root generated target should not reference the application's default target as an automatic dependency.

Given a package that explicitly declares `cpp_info.requires` on a specific component exported by a package marked as `application`, when its CMake targets are generated, that explicit component target should still appear as a dependency.
When a required package is not marked as `application`, `CMakeConfigDeps` should continue generating dependency references for it according to the existing rules.

task_20.title: Improve cc compiler version auto-detection
task_20.description: The upgrade improves automatic compiler detection for `cc` so it can parse more real-world gcc and clang version outputs and still detect the compiler when the executable path needs quoting. This reduces incorrect or missing compiler version detection during profile or environment discovery.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that automatic `cc` compiler detection correctly identifies the compiler version for common gcc and clang `--version` outputs, including outputs that include parenthesized build metadata before the version number, outputs that expose only a major or major.minor version, and compiler executable paths that require quoting.

expectation.grounded: When Conan detects a compiler through the `cc` executable, it should invoke `<compiler_exe> --version` safely even if the executable path contains spaces or requires shell quoting. It should continue to classify the compiler as `clang` when the version output identifies clang and as `gcc` otherwise, and it should extract the installed version from the first valid compiler version token even when parenthesized build metadata appears before that token or when the reported version has only one or two numeric components.
expectation.conceptual: Automatic compiler detection should accept the version formats commonly emitted by wrapped or toolchain-provided `cc` compilers and return the correct compiler family and version instead of failing or misreading metadata as the version.

constraints.grounded: Detection must continue to return no detected compiler information when invoking `--version` fails, must preserve successful parsing of already supported multi-segment version formats, and must not change the existing gcc-versus-clang classification behavior beyond the improved version extraction.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should broaden supported `cc` outputs without changing established detection behavior for already supported compilers or turning failed compiler invocations into successful detections.

behavior: Version detection for `cc` recognizes numeric versions with one, two, or more components, such as major-only, major.minor, and major.minor.patch forms.
When `cc --version` output includes parenthesized build or toolchain metadata before the compiler version, detection skips that metadata and captures the actual compiler version that follows it.
Compiler detection invokes the compiler executable as a quoted path, allowing version detection to succeed when the executable path contains spaces or otherwise requires shell-safe quoting.
acceptance_criteria: When automatic compiler detection reads a `cc --version` output where parenthesized build metadata precedes the numeric compiler version, it should report the numeric compiler version that follows the metadata.
When automatic compiler detection reads a `cc --version` output that exposes only a major version such as `18`, it should accept that as the installed compiler version.
When automatic compiler detection reads a `cc --version` output that exposes a major.minor version such as `14.2`, it should accept that as the installed compiler version.

When the configured `cc` executable path contains spaces, automatic compiler detection should still execute `--version` successfully and return the detected compiler family and version if the compiler responds successfully.
When invoking the `cc` executable for version detection fails, automatic compiler detection should continue to report no detected compiler information rather than a partial or guessed result.

task_21.title: Honor Apple deployment targets in XcodeBuild invocations
task_21.description: Conan 2.19.0 fixes Apple XcodeBuild integration so builds inherit the deployment target defined in the Conan profile and safely pass project and target names that contain spaces or similar shell-sensitive characters.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Apple builds launched through Conan's XcodeBuild helper use the deployment target configured in the profile and handle project paths and target names safely when invoking xcodebuild.

expectation.grounded: When `conan.tools.apple.XcodeBuild.build()` is used for Apple platforms and `settings.os.version` is defined, the generated `xcodebuild` invocation should include the matching deployment target variable for the selected `settings.os`: `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` for `Macos`, `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` for `iOS`, `TVOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` for `tvOS`, `WATCHOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` for `watchOS`, and `XROS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` for `visionOS`. The `-project` argument value and the optional `-target` value should be quoted so Xcode project paths and target names are passed as single arguments.
expectation.conceptual: Xcode-based Apple builds should reflect the minimum OS version declared in the user's Conan profile, and build commands should remain valid even when project or target names contain spaces.

constraints.grounded: Do not append any deployment target variable when `settings.os.version` is absent or when the selected OS does not map to an Apple deployment target key. Preserve existing `XcodeBuild.build()` behavior for configuration, architecture, SDK-related arguments, verbosity, and the use of `-alltargets` when no target is supplied.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only add the appropriate deployment target when the profile provides one and should not alter unrelated build options or change how builds behave when no explicit target is requested.

behavior: `XcodeBuild.build()` now propagates the profile's Apple deployment target into the launched `xcodebuild` command when both `settings.os` and `settings.os.version` identify a supported Apple platform.
Deployment target propagation covers `Macos`, `iOS`, `tvOS`, `watchOS`, and `visionOS`, each using its platform-specific deployment target variable name.
If `settings.os.version` is missing, `XcodeBuild.build()` does not add any deployment target assignment to the `xcodebuild` invocation.
The Xcode project path passed to `-project` is quoted before invoking `xcodebuild`.
When a target name is provided, the value passed to `-target` is quoted before invoking `xcodebuild`.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan profile sets `os=Macos` and `os.version` to a specific version, a build executed through `XcodeBuild.build()` should invoke `xcodebuild` with `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` set to that version.

When a Conan profile sets `os` to `iOS`, `tvOS`, `watchOS`, or `visionOS` and provides `os.version`, a build executed through `XcodeBuild.build()` should invoke `xcodebuild` with the corresponding platform deployment target variable set to that version.
When `settings.os.version` is not provided, `XcodeBuild.build()` should invoke `xcodebuild` without adding an Apple deployment target variable.
When the Xcode project path contains spaces, invoking `XcodeBuild.build()` should still pass the project path correctly to `xcodebuild` as a single argument.
When a target name contains spaces, invoking `XcodeBuild.build()` with that target should still pass the target name correctly to `xcodebuild` as a single argument.

task_22.title: Honor deployment targets and preserve spaced XcodeBuild arguments
task_22.description: The `XcodeBuild` helper now forwards the Apple deployment target from the configured profile into the generated `xcodebuild` invocation and quotes the project path and explicit target name so builds keep working when those values contain spaces.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `XcodeBuild` honors the deployment target declared in the Apple profile and correctly handles Xcode project paths or target names that contain spaces.

expectation.grounded: `XcodeBuild.build()` should invoke `xcodebuild` with the `-project` value treated as a single argument and, when a `target` is provided, the `-target` value treated as a single argument as well. When the active Apple settings resolve to a deployment target key and `os.version` is set, the generated command should also include that deployment target assignment using the configured version. If `target` is omitted, the existing `-alltargets` behavior should remain. If no deployment target key is available or `os.version` is unset, no deployment target assignment should be emitted.
expectation.conceptual: Building through `XcodeBuild` should preserve project and target names exactly, including spaces, and Apple builds should automatically respect the deployment target specified in the user's profile whenever one is available.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing `XcodeBuild` command composition intact for configuration, architecture, SDK, verbosity, and all-target builds. Limit the change to safe handling of project and target arguments and conditional forwarding of the deployment target only when profile data provides a usable OS version.
constraints.conceptual: Do not alter unrelated build options or require new inputs. Builds without a deployment target should continue to run as before, and builds with spaces in names should no longer be misparsed by the command line.

behavior: `XcodeBuild.build()` treats the supplied Xcode project path as one `-project` argument, preventing spaces in the path from splitting the command.
When a target name is supplied, `XcodeBuild.build()` treats it as one `-target` argument, preventing spaces in the target name from being split.
When the active Apple profile includes `os.version`, `XcodeBuild.build()` forwards the matching deployment target setting to `xcodebuild` using that version.
When no target name is supplied, `XcodeBuild.build()` continues to request an all-target build.
When the profile does not provide a usable deployment target version, no deployment target setting is added to the `xcodebuild` invocation.
acceptance_criteria: When `XcodeBuild` is used with an Xcode project path containing spaces, it should pass the full path as the project value instead of splitting it across arguments.
When `XcodeBuild` is used with an explicit target name containing spaces, it should pass the full target name as a single target value.
When an Apple profile defines `os.version`, the resulting `xcodebuild` invocation should include the corresponding deployment target for that platform using the configured version.
When no `target` is specified, `XcodeBuild` should still perform an all-target build.
When `os.version` is not set, the resulting build command should omit deployment target forwarding.

task_23.title: Stabilize configuration package IDs against config_mode
task_23.description: Conan 2.19.0 fixes configuration-package package ID handling. Packages declared with `package_type="configuration"`, including config installation packages, no longer have their own binary identity changed by `core.package_id:config_mode`, preventing unnecessary binary variation while preserving config-mode behavior for other package types.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that packages declared with `package_type="configuration"` keep a stable `package_id` that does not depend on `core.package_id:config_mode`, so configuration packages do not produce different binaries or become coupled to configuration-version changes when they are created or installed.

expectation.grounded: When Conan evaluates the `package_id` of a package whose declared `package_type` is `configuration`, it must not apply the `config_mode` contribution from `core.package_id:config_mode` to that package's own binary identity. Observable outcomes that depend on the resolved `package_id`, including which binary package reference is created or selected, should therefore remain unchanged for the configuration package itself when only configuration-version inputs vary. Packages of other types should continue to use the configured `config_mode` behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Configuration packages should have a stable binary identity of their own instead of changing with configuration-version tracking. After upgrading, these packages should be reusable across config-mode settings, while non-configuration packages should continue to behave as before.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove `core.package_id:config_mode` handling globally. The exemption applies only to packages whose declared `package_type` is `configuration`, and only to that package's own `package_id` evaluation. Existing package ID semantics for non-configuration packages and unrelated package ID inputs must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the fix narrowly scoped to configuration packages. Other packages must retain their current package identity rules, and the change must not broadly disable configuration-based package version tracking.

behavior: A package declared with `package_type="configuration"` no longer incorporates configuration-version influence into its own `package_id` when `core.package_id:config_mode` is set.
Creating or resolving a configuration package yields the same binary identity regardless of the configured `config_mode` value for that package.
Non-configuration packages continue to follow the configured `core.package_id:config_mode` rules.
acceptance_criteria: When `core.package_id:config_mode` is configured and a package with `package_type="configuration"` is created or installed, its resolved `package_id` should not change solely because configuration-version data for that package exists or changes.
When configuration-version inputs for a configuration package change, Conan should not create or select a different binary for that configuration package only because of `config_mode` processing.
When a package is not a configuration package, Conan should continue to apply `core.package_id:config_mode` as before.

task_24.title: Fix PremakeDeps dependency link ordering
task_24.description: Conan 2.19.0 fixes PremakeDeps so generated Premake dependency setup preserves a deterministic dependency-aware library link order for each build configuration. This prevents link failures on order-sensitive linkers when one library depends on another library that would otherwise appear too early or too late in the link line.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that projects using PremakeDeps link Conan dependencies in a deterministic dependency-aware order so dependent libraries are linked before the libraries they require, avoiding linker failures on order-sensitive linkers and preserving correct behavior across build configurations.

expectation.grounded: `PremakeDeps` must generate Premake dependency metadata that records an explicit library order for each configuration and make `conan_setup_build(conf)` consume that order when linking all packages for a configuration. The generated output should include a root `conanconfig.premake5.lua` and configuration-specific `conanconfig_<config>.premake5.lua` files, and the recorded order for each configuration should follow dependency topology so more dependent libraries are linked before their prerequisites.
expectation.conceptual: Using PremakeDeps should automatically produce stable, correct link ordering. Consumers should not need to manually reorder Conan-provided libraries, and each generated build configuration should keep its own dependency order data.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing `PremakeDeps` entry point and full-configuration setup behavior while making link order deterministic. Ordering data must remain configuration-specific, support repeated generation of different configurations without losing earlier configuration data, and continue to work with Premake dependency metadata merging.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be additive and non-disruptive: existing Premake integration should continue to work, multiple generated configurations should coexist, and the main behavior change should be corrected link ordering.

behavior: `PremakeDeps` now derives dependency iteration for link setup from dependency topology instead of unordered dependency table traversal.
Generated Premake metadata now includes per-configuration dependency-order data through `conanconfig_<config>.premake5.lua` files aggregated by `conanconfig.premake5.lua`.

When `conan_setup_build(conf)` is invoked without a specific package, it links libraries by iterating the recorded ordered list for that configuration instead of iterating an unordered dependency table.

The resulting link order places libraries with downstream dependencies earlier than the libraries they depend on, fixing unresolved symbol scenarios on order-sensitive linkers such as GNU `ld` and `gold`.
Generating an additional configuration preserves previously generated configuration-order includes so multiple configurations remain available.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer uses PremakeDeps with a dependency chain where one library requires another, the generated Premake setup should link the requiring library before its prerequisite library.

When `conan_setup_build(<configuration>)` is used to apply all dependencies for a configuration, the libraries should be linked in a deterministic order derived from dependency relationships rather than unordered table iteration.

When building on Linux with order-sensitive linkers such as GNU `ld` or `gold`, dependency graphs that previously required manual link reordering should link successfully with the generated Conan Premake files alone.

When PremakeDeps outputs more than one build configuration over time, the shared Premake config entry point should continue to include the configuration-specific order data for both old and new configurations.
